title: Reading and writing files
summary: Read a text file with fs.readFileSync, process its lines and save a result with fs.writeFileSync.

quiz.q: fs.readFileSync('notes.txt') with no second argument returns what?
quiz.explain: Without an encoding Node cannot know the file holds text, so it gives you raw bytes in a `Buffer`. Pass `'utf8'` as the second argument to get a string.

quiz.q: Complete the line that reads a file as text.
quiz.explain: `readFileSync(path, 'utf8')` reads the whole file and returns it as a string.

quiz.q: The file list.txt contains the three lines `a`, `b` and `c`, each followed by a newline. How many items does this array have?
quiz.explain:
The text is `a
b
c
`. Splitting on `
` also creates an empty item after the last newline. Remove empty lines with `.filter(Boolean)` or `.trim()` the text first.

quiz.q: What does fs.writeFileSync('out.txt', 'Hi') do if out.txt already has content?
options: Throws an error because the file exists
Replaces the old content with Hi
quiz.explain: `writeFileSync` overwrites. To add to the end of a file use `fs.appendFileSync`.

exercise.task:
The folder contains `marks.txt` with one student per line, written as `name,mark`, for example `Asha,82`.

In `report.js`, read `marks.txt` and write a file `summary.txt` with exactly these three lines:

```
Students: 3
Average: 80
Top: Meena
```

- `Students` is the number of students, `Average` is the average mark and `Top` is the name with the highest mark.
- Your program must work for any `marks.txt`, not only this one. Ignore empty lines.
- Use the relative file names `marks.txt` and `summary.txt`.
hints: Read the file with `fs.readFileSync('marks.txt', 'utf8')`, split it into lines, then split each line on the comma.

Remember the empty last line: `.trim().split('\n')`. Turn the mark into a number with `Number(...)`. Keep the best student in a variable while you loop. Build the output as one string with `\n` between lines.
